desc: Verify the coloring reduction on the samples by hand and formalize the parity-fix algorithm (top-2K by m_i, parity classes, flexible-type enumeration, O(1) fix patterns with precomputed candidates)

Build a brute-force checker (exhaustive over subsets/colorings for N ≤ 10) and stress-test the greedy+fix solution against it, including duplicate values, all-equal m, single flexible cake, and K = N/2 edge cases; run both samples

Prove or brute-force-verify that the enumerated parity-fix patterns are complete, especially: whether 2 actions always suffice, and whether two swap actions can illegally reuse the same inside/outside item (may need top-2 candidates per class with conflict checks)
Fix any bugs found by stress testing (e.g., add top-2 candidate handling for swap conflicts, correct flex_feasible edge cases) and re-verify
Run a final large-N performance sanity check (N=1e5, random values) to confirm speed, and do a final code review of edge cases (O empty, best_in=-1 guards, no-flexible cases)
Finalize the solution: per test case O(N log N), Python ints, fast I/O via sys.stdin.buffer
